Sequences

An intro's order lives on its section. data-fh-intro marks the owner; data-fh-enter-children staggers a list by --fh-stagger (60ms). The homepage hero is written exactly this way.

_firehorse

The design system

that moves the same everywhere.

  • Tokens
  • Entrances
  • Sequences
  • Scroll
  • Choreography
  • Drift

Scroll-linked

CSS only, on the page's scroll timeline: it tracks the scroll exactly and costs no script per frame. Scroll the page and watch these.

fh-recede
fh-scroll-fade
fh-reveal
fh-parallax

Page progress: <div class="fh-scroll-progress"></div> draws the line at the top of this page.

Choreography

Script measures once and on resize; the motion itself still runs on the scroll timeline. The circle reveal, glide and lock are free in the enhancer (firehorse.js); dock beside is Firehorse Pro. See them together on the homepage concept.

Circle revealFree · Firehorse.reveal(change, from)
GlideFree · data-fh-glide="center" <nav><div data-fh-glide="center">…links…</div></nav>
LockFree · data-fh-lock <h1 data-fh-lock="clone" data-fh-lock-to=".nav a" data-fh-lock-scale="0.78" data-fh-lock-href="#top">
Dock beside Prodata-fh-dock-beside="#cta" <div class="tools" data-fh-dock-beside=".cta">

Drift

A photo shows a set share at a time; the rest rests under a soft veil and drifts in, so the photo's tone holds. Five styles are free, three are Pro. import { createDrift } from "/drift.js".

Tokens

Every timing comes from a token; no component or page writes its own milliseconds or curves.

--fh-ease-out
--fh-ease-expo-out
--fh-ease-in-out
--fh-ease-spring
--fh-ease-glide
--fh-ease-in

Durations: instant 80ms · fast 150ms · base 220ms · slow 420ms · enter 600ms · reveal 720ms · intro 900ms · scene 1.1s. Beat 150ms · stagger 60ms · rise 0.6rem · recede to 0.9.

Rules

The same seven hold for every piece; the agent contract carries them.

  1. Reduced motion wins. Everything appears in place; scroll pieces hold still; Drift shows one still frame.
  2. Content is never parked. Without script nothing is hidden; intros run only with fh-js and fh-ready arrives within 2s.
  3. Transform and opacity only. Clips and masks for draws and wipes; never width, height, top, left or margins.
  4. Tokens only. A new timing becomes a token first.
  5. One owner per sequence. The order lives on its section.
  6. Scroll-linked on the compositor. Script measures once and on resize, never per frame.
  7. Budget. No live blur on large or fixed surfaces; loops pause off screen; Drift runs at about 30fps.

families.name: Etched split
families.summary: A full-bleed pair that breaks out of the content column while its copy still lines up with the content edge on both sides. Stacks when the page is narrow. --roomy gives each pane the full section rhythm. Cinch is built on it.
families.markup:
Why it matters

Most systems fail at the seams, not the center

Each tool works on its own. The cost shows up where data crosses from one to the next: re-keyed orders, stale reports, follow-ups nobody owns.

The approach

  • Map every hand-off between systems
  • Fix the model before adding automation
  • Instrument it so problems surface first

groups.name: Dictation
groups.summary: Type or talk. The label and a Text | Transcribe switch share the first row; while listening, a live caption shows the waveform, clock and interim words. Progressive: without the switch it is a plain textarea. Wire with data-fh-dictate (or drive the same markup yourself).

groups.name: Quiet
groups.summary: A barely-there lift off the canvas, no border. Default fields already use a light fill (--fh-color-field); quiet is fainter still. Use fh-field--quiet or fh-input--quiet.

groups.name: Password reveal
groups.summary: A show and hide toggle inside a password field. Put the input in an fh-input-group and add an fh-input-reveal button after it. firehorse.js switches the input between hidden and plain text, keeps aria-pressed and the label in step, and hides the value again when the form submits.

groups.name: Money input
groups.summary: A currency prefix, or a select when several currencies are allowed, then a text input with inputmode="decimal" (never type="number": no spinner). money.js groups digits as you type and keeps a hidden input in step that posts whole minor units, so 1,250.00 posts 125000. Without the script the field posts what was typed. Add data-allow-negative to allow a minus sign.
